subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after the sessions.activity API lands, or should core stop at activity/diagnostic signals for plugins and dashboards to consume?
rationale: The request adds new feature, config, delivery, privacy, UI/operator, and optional model-call behavior rather than repairing an existing contract, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary.

options.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
options.body: Keep this issue open as the downstream product/design item once the canonical sessions.activity contract is settled.

options.title: Route alerting to plugins or dashboards
options.body: Close or redirect this if maintainers want core to expose activity and diagnostics only while external or plugin-owned surfaces handle alert delivery.

options.title: Limit core to diagnostics-only alerts
options.body: Keep a narrower core issue for structured diagnostic events without channel/webhook delivery or model summaries.

recommendation.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the downstream product/design item once the canonical sessions.activity contract is settled.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current-history signal around gateway/session, protocol, and adjacent operator visibility surfaces.
